title: What is a Dead Letter Queue (DLQ)?
description: Explain why messages may be moved to a DLQ.
answer: A Dead Letter Queue stores messages that cannot be processed successfully after configured attempts or because of a non-retryable error. It helps isolate poison messages, inspect failures, and replay messages after fixing the issue. Configure alerting, retention, and a safe redrive process.

title: What is cache invalidation?
description: Describe common strategies for keeping cached data consistent with its source.
answer: Cache invalidation removes or refreshes cached entries when source data changes. Common approaches include time-to-live (TTL), explicit eviction after writes, write-through, and event-driven invalidation. Choose a strategy based on freshness requirements and acceptable staleness.

title: What is the role of an API Gateway?
description: Explain common responsibilities of a gateway in a microservices architecture.
answer: An API Gateway provides a client-facing entry point and can route requests to services, terminate TLS, enforce authentication and rate limits, and handle cross-cutting concerns. Avoid turning it into a place for extensive business logic, and consider resilience, observability, and gateway availability.
